title: The Day the Clipboard Arrived
skyStory: December arrives and the half moon is sitting in Virgo with a clipboard, checking the year off line by line. Thirty-one boxes left. It has already alphabetized the stars and is now judging Orion's belt for being slightly crooked. Saturn approves of the paperwork. Mars wants to know who invited the clipboard. The wind off the water rattles the window like it wants to help.

reading: The last month of the year opens and the Fire Tiger immediately starts a list titled Before January. It already has fourteen items. The Virgo moon wants you to cross three of them off, not add a fifteenth. The [[Knight of Wands]] agrees and is tapping its hoof at item two.

Around 11:40 am someone will ask how you are and actually wait for the answer. Give a real one, not the usual busy-good-busy. The cabin has a fresh stack of firewood by the door this week, and nobody chopped it but you. Picture yourself sitting next to it for one full minute. A builder is allowed to admire the woodpile.
joel.mission: Cross three things off a list today with a pen that has a satisfying click, then retire the pen somewhere ceremonial.
joel.omen: A sticky note clinging to the bottom of a shoe. A forgotten idea is trying to hitch a ride back to you.
joel.stoneWhy: Virgo likes things solid and black
joel.elementWhy: lists need ground to stand on

reading: Capricorn season is three weeks away and you can already hear it backstage, tuning up like a small orchestra. The Mountain does not rush December. You let it come to you one quiet morning at a time, and you remember which mornings were the good ones.

Somebody will bring you a tangled problem today, the kind with three knots and a mystery fourth. The Wood Rat spots the fourth knot first. Point at it gently. Do not untie it for them. Hand it back with one hint and watch their face when it clicks. That face is your favourite kind of thank-you note.
nancy.mission: Help someone level up one tiny skill today, then slip away before they can thank you properly.
nancy.omen: A single red mitten on a fence post. Someone is saving you a seat you did not know about.
nancy.stoneWhy: a calm tide for a busy desk
nancy.elementWhy: fresh December air clears the clutter

together.text: Each of you write the one word you want December to be about on a scrap of paper. Swap scraps. Keep the other person's word in a pocket all month. The Virgo moon will audit your pockets on New Year's Eve, and it absolutely will check.

title: The Day of the Rogue Label Maker
skyStory: The moon is still parked in Virgo, a little thinner, and it has found a label maker. Everything in the sky is getting a sticker. The Big Dipper now says SOUP. Venus got one that just says NO. Saturn asked for a label and was told it already is one. The moon is shrinking, but its confidence is not.

reading: Mars has woken up feeling cheeky and wants you to rename something. A folder, a playlist, a houseplant, the drawer where cables go to hibernate. The name you choose will stick for years, so choose one that makes you laugh every time you see it.

Your Life Path 3 is buzzing around 2 pm, right when a meeting or a chat goes quiet and awkward. Fill the silence with exactly one good question and then stop talking. The [[Page of Wands]] is watching to see whether you can light a spark and walk away from it. You can. Look how calm the Tiger is. Mostly calm. The tail is twitching a little.
joel.mission: Give a ridiculous new name to one everyday object at home and use that name out loud at least twice.
joel.omen: A dog wearing a sweater nicer than yours. Your style is about to get a compliment from a surprising direction.
joel.stoneWhy: Nancy's fire keeps your wit warm

reading: Low tide energy today, in the best way. Things that were hidden under the water are showing themselves, like that idea you parked in October and forgot about. It has barnacles on it now. It is also better than you remembered.

At some point your hands will start telling a story before your mouth catches up. Let them lead. The diamond on your left ring finger catches the light at the punchline, and somebody across the room will laugh without having heard the beginning. That is how good the hands are. Saturn, your old ruler, is pretending to read a newspaper, but it is grinning behind it.
nancy.mission: Dig up one idea you shelved this autumn and tell it to someone out loud, barnacles and all.
nancy.omen: A heron standing perfectly still in a half-frozen ditch, ignoring everybody. A messy situation is about to sort itself out without you lifting a finger.

together.text: Each of you invents a fake holiday for December 2nd and texts the other the official rules. Minimum one required hat. Maximum one required dance. Whoever's holiday is sillier gets to declare it observed annually, effective immediately.

title: The Day of the Wobbly Scales
skyStory: A quarter-lit crescent drifts into Libra, which hands it a set of golden scales and says please keep things even. The moon tries. It puts a snowflake on one side and a snowflake on the other. One of them melts. Libra sighs a deeply diplomatic sigh. Mars and Saturn are asked to sit on opposite ends of the seesaw, and for one shining minute nobody tips over.

reading: Libra is asking the giver in you an awkward question: what did you get this week? Not what did you give. Get. If the answer is a blank, the [[Six of Pentacles]] has been stacking small gifts outside the cabin door and you keep stepping over them.

Today, pick one up. A compliment, a coffee, a hand with a heavy thing. Say thank you and nothing else. No but-you-shouldn't-have, no I'll-get-the-next-one. Just the two words, then a pause long enough for the other person to feel good about it. The chimney puffs out one smug little smoke ring. It knows you can do this.
joel.mission: Accept one offer of help today without arguing, bargaining, or immediately paying it back.
joel.omen: Two crows sharing one branch without squabbling. Somebody is about to meet you exactly halfway.

reading: The Wood Rat wakes up already knowing who in the room is quietly struggling. You always do. Libra wants you to balance that gift with one rule today: help them, then help yourself to something equally nice afterwards. Equal scales.

Around 4:15 pm the light will go gold and sideways the way it only does in early December. Stop whatever you are doing and look at it for the length of one breath. The ruby on your right pinky will glow a deeper shade of purple-pink, which is Joel's fire saying it noticed the light too, from wherever it is.
nancy.mission: For every kind thing you do for someone today, do one equally kind thing for yourself. Keep score.
nancy.omen: A perfectly balanced stack of rocks or plates somewhere unexpected. You are closer to even than you think.
nancy.stoneWhy: Joel's fire on a cold afternoon

together.text: Libra wants fairness, so today you trade one small chore or errand. Whoever usually does the thing hands it over. Whoever never does it learns it badly. Nobody is allowed to correct the technique. The scales wobble, then settle, then giggle.

title: The Day of the Matching Scarves
skyStory: A slim crescent lingers in Libra, still holding the scales, and the universe decides today it will balance things in the strangest way possible: by making pairs. Two of everything. Twin clouds. Twin puddles. Twin strangers in identical hats at the same bus stop. The moon claims it had nothing to do with it. Nobody believes the moon.

reading: Something will happen in twos today, and the second one will be so precise you will stop mid-step. It might be the same odd word said by two people an hour apart, or the same song in two shops. When it happens, you are contractually obligated to text Nancy one word: DES.

The Tiger loves a sign, and Libra is handing them out like party favours. Do not try to decode it. The point is not the meaning; the point is the grin. The [[Wheel of Fortune]] has spun twice on the same number today, and the house is laughing along with you, not at you.
joel.mission: When the double coincidence lands, take a photo of the second half and send it to Nancy with zero context.
joel.omen: Two snowplows passing each other with their blades raised like a salute. Don't even scream; just count the next pair you see.

reading: Your Life Path 11 is literally two ones standing side by side, so today belongs to you more than anyone. The universe is running a doubles tournament and you are the referee. You will spot the pairs before anybody else does, and you will be smug about it.

Around midday you will see someone wearing the exact scarf you were thinking about buying, or the exact colour you were going to wear tomorrow. Then, by evening, a second person in the same thing. ΔΕΣ, absolutely. The pearl on your right ring finger, a little moon of its own, glows like it was in on the joke all along.
nancy.mission: Keep a tally of every pair you notice before bedtime. Report the final number to Joel like a sports score.
nancy.omen: Two gulls landing at the same instant on two posts. The 11 in you is being waved at.
nancy.stoneWhy: a little moon holding the joke
nancy.elementWhy: the tide repeats itself on purpose

together.text: DES day. Before dark, each of you independently picks a random object and texts it to the other at exactly 8:11 pm. Do not coordinate. Do not hint. If you both pick something from the same room of a house, the universe owes you each a cookie.

title: The Day of the Secret Drawer
skyStory: The crescent is thinning to a sliver and has slipped into Scorpio, which immediately dims the lights and lowers its voice. Scorpio knows where everything is hidden. The moon now wears a tiny trench coat. It is asking pointed questions of Mercury, who is sweating. Somewhere a drawer that never quite closes is humming to itself. Mars approves. Mars loves a mystery.

reading: Scorpio moon digs. Today it is digging around in the cabin's back room, the one with the half-finished projects. It pulls out one of them, blows off the dust, and sets it on the table. Not to make you finish it. Just to ask you, honestly, whether you still want to.

If the answer is no, you are allowed to let it go. Say goodbye like a gentleman, maybe a little bow. If the answer is yes, give it ten minutes today and no more. The [[Knight of Wands]] wants one fire, aimed properly, not ten fires smoking politely in the yard. Courage today is choosing, not starting.
joel.mission: Choose one unfinished project and either give it ten honest minutes or formally retire it with a small bow.
joel.omen: A key you do not recognize in a pocket or a drawer. A door you forgot about wants opening again.
joel.stoneWhy: clear eyes for the back room

reading: Scorpio and the Wood Rat get along suspiciously well. Both of you see straight through people, kindly. Today somebody will tell you one thing and mean another, and you will hear the second thing clear as a bell. Answer the second thing.

Around 3 pm a small truth will come out of hiding. Maybe a coworker admits they need help. Maybe you admit you would like a nap shaped like a whole weekend. Either way, the onyx at your left wrist hums a low note. It was Joel's stone first, and it has picked up the Tiger's habit of saying things straight. Let it.
nancy.mission: Answer the question underneath a question someone asks you today, gently and directly.
nancy.omen: A black cat sitting perfectly still in a window. It is not bad luck; it is a fellow detective saluting you.

together.text: Scorpio wants one honest thing from each of you. Tell the other one small truth you have been sitting on: a favourite memory, a tiny worry, a ridiculous dream. No fixing allowed. The listener just says thank you, then names the bravest word in it.

title: The Day of the Five Percent Moon
skyStory: Only five percent of the moon is left showing, a silver eyelash in Scorpio. It is about to vanish for a few days, and Scorpio has convinced it to clean house before it goes. Old grudges, expired coupons, that one email draft from March: out. The sky looks lighter already. Saturn holds the trash bag open with dignity.

reading: The moon is nearly empty, and that is the whole lesson. You cannot pour fresh fire into a full lantern. Today the Tiger is allowed to put something down. A worry you have been carrying for someone else. A promise you made to yourself that has gone stale and itchy.

Pick one and drop it on purpose. Out loud helps. Say I am not carrying this into the new moon, and then go do something noisy and fun. The [[Eight of Swords]] cage was always made of thoughts, and five percent moonlight is enough to show you the door was never locked. Walk out whistling.
joel.mission: Write one stale worry on a scrap of paper, crumple it, and toss it into a bin from at least three steps away.
joel.omen: A balloon drifting loose above a parking lot. Something you let go of today will not come back, and good.

reading: The tide is going way, way out today, farther than usual, and it is taking a few things with it. Let it. You have been carrying the [[Six of Swords]] boat's oars for a while now, and Joel keeps offering to row. Today, let Joel take one oar.

Not literally, unless there is a boat available, in which case absolutely yes. Mostly it means letting somebody help with one heavy thing this week. The stacked diamonds on your left middle finger flash like a lighthouse every time you gesture, which is often, which means the lighthouse is working overtime. Give the keeper a break.
nancy.mission: Hand one task or worry to someone you trust today and do not take it back before bedtime.
nancy.omen: A piece of driftwood shaped like a letter. That letter is the first initial of something you are ready to finish.

together.text: Before the moon goes dark, each of you names one thing you are leaving in 2026's lost-and-found. Say it to each other. Then, in unison, a small dramatic wave goodbye. The wave can be in person, on a call or in a text with too many hand emojis.

title: The Day the Arrow Left the Bow
skyStory: New moon in Sagittarius. The sky goes dark and quiet, and then Sagittarius, the archer, draws a bow with no arrow in it and points it at the horizon. The arrow, apparently, is you. Both of you. Mars cheers loudly. Saturn checks the aim twice. Somewhere behind the clouds, a fresh cycle cracks its knuckles and stretches.

reading: A new moon in the sign of adventure, and the Fire Tiger is pacing the edge of the woods with its ears up. Seeds planted now grow fast. So plant exactly one. Not a garden. One seed, labelled clearly, so you can find it again in January.

The [[Ace of Wands]] is sitting on your windowsill like a lit match that refuses to go out. Pick something that scares you a little and excites you a lot: a class, a project, a message you have been drafting in your head since summer. Write the first line. Just the first line, in the dark of the moon, while nobody is watching. Tomorrow it will still be there.
joel.mission: Write the first sentence of something brand new and put the date on it. Nothing more today.
joel.omen: An arrow painted on a road or a sign pointing somewhere unexpected. Follow it with your eyes and smile.
joel.stoneWhy: a new moon wants a little moon
joel.elementWhy: the first spark of the cycle

reading: Sagittarius wants to go on a trip, and the Wood Rat has already packed snacks. A new moon is the perfect moment to set an intention, and yours is probably something sensible and quietly enormous, the way all your plans are.

Here is the twist: make it a little less sensible. Add one wild detail. If you were going to read more, read something strange. If you were going to rest, rest somewhere new. Saturn loves your discipline. Sagittarius wants to see your mischief. The ruby on your right pinky is Joel's fire, and it votes for mischief every time.
nancy.mission: Set one intention for this moon cycle and add a single ridiculous detail to it before you write it down.
nancy.omen: A map, a globe or a travel poster in an unlikely place. Your intention has an adventure inside it.

together.text: New moon pact. Each of you names one seed you are planting this cycle and one way the other can cheer it on. Write both down somewhere you will find again on the full moon of December 23rd. Seal it with an air high-five.

title: The Day of Zero Percent
skyStory: Zero percent illumination. The moon is completely hidden in Sagittarius, technically there, practically on vacation. It has left an out-of-office note: back soon, do not do anything I would not do. Considering it is a Sagittarius moon, that leaves a lot of room. The stars, unsupervised, are rearranging themselves into a tiny cabin and a tiny shore.

reading: With no moon in the sky, the cabin is the only light for miles, and the chimney is doing its best impression of a lighthouse. Tonight is for staying in. Thick socks. A warm mug. A book you have been meaning to open since August.

The Tiger thinks rest is a waste of a perfectly good evening. The Tiger is wrong tonight. The [[Four of Swords]] has made up the cot by the woodstove and fluffed the pillow. A builder sharpens the axe before chopping more wood, and you sharpen yours by doing absolutely nothing for one whole evening. Let the dark hold you for a bit. It is good at it.
joel.mission: Pick one evening hour to do nothing productive at all. If guilt shows up, offer it a blanket too.
joel.omen: A porch light clicking on by itself as you walk past. Someone is thinking warmly of you right now.
joel.stoneWhy: dark stone for a dark sky
joel.elementWhy: let the gale do the work

reading: The shore at new moon is the darkest it gets, and the waves sound louder because there is nothing to look at. You hear better in the dark. You always have. Tonight something you have been half-listening to will become clear.

Maybe it is a decision about how to spend the holidays. Maybe it is just which blanket is the best blanket. Either way, you will know by 9:30 pm, and you will be right, because the Wood Rat does not guess. The diamond on your left ring finger catches the lamp and throws one tiny star on the ceiling. Wish on it. It counts.
nancy.mission: Turn off every light but one for twenty minutes tonight and listen to the house settle around you.
nancy.omen: A dripping tap that stops the moment you notice it. Something you were waiting on is about to resolve.
nancy.stoneWhy: your own star on the ceiling

together.text: No missions tonight, only a ritual. At the same time, each of you lights a candle or turns on one warm lamp and texts the other a photo of it. Two small lights in the longest-dark month. The sky has no moon, so you are it.

title: The Day of the Snowball Dare
skyStory: One percent of a moon, peeking out of Sagittarius like a kid hiding behind a snowbank with a snowball. It has excellent aim and absolutely no remorse. Jupiter, the archer's ruler, is egging it on from the sidelines. Saturn has put on a helmet. Mars has already thrown one back. The first real snow of the season is rumoured in the forecast, and the moon is taking credit early.

reading: A Sagittarius sky loves a bold move, and the Tiger is feeling sporty. Today you will be tempted to say yes to something slightly out of your lane. A new route home, a weird lunch spot, a conversation with the quiet person in the corner. Say yes.

Around 1:20 pm the day will try to get boring on you. Do not let it. Change one tiny thing: stand up for the next call, switch which hand holds your mug, take the stairs two at a time. The [[Knight of Wands]] is galloping beside you and wants to see some dust kicked up. Small chaos, kindly done, is a Fire Tiger specialty.
joel.mission: Take a completely different route somewhere you go every day, and spot one thing you have never noticed.
joel.omen: A child's mitten frozen into the shape of a wave on a railing. Keep going; you are being cheered on.

reading: The Wood Rat has a plan, and Sagittarius wants to throw a snowball at it. Not to wreck it. Just to see what you do when a plan gets a little wet and lumpy. You will do great. You always improvise better than you think you will.

When the hiccup comes, probably mid-afternoon and probably involving a calendar, take a breath and grin. You know three backup routes nobody else considered. The pearl on your right ring finger is water, and water always finds the way around a rock. Tell the story of the hiccup later with full hand gestures. It will be funnier than the original plan.
nancy.mission: When a plan changes today, say out loud: wonderful, a plot twist. Mean it at least a little.
nancy.omen: Footprints in fresh snow that suddenly turn sideways. A detour is about to be the good part.

together.text: Dare exchange. Each of you dares the other to do one small brave thing before Friday: sing in the car with the window down, compliment a stranger's boots, try a new recipe. Report back with evidence. Courage counts double when witnessed.

title: The Day the Moon Came Home
skyStory: The new moon tiptoes out of Sagittarius and into Capricorn, Nancy's own sign, still almost invisible at two percent. It knocks on the Mountain's door with snow on its boots. Saturn opens it, wearing slippers and a cardigan, and says: you are late, there is soup. The moon is very happy to be home. Everyone pretends not to cry.

reading: The moon is visiting Nancy's sign, which means the whole sky is a little more patient, a little more steady and a little more likely to tell you to finish what you started. The cabin likes this weather. The kettle is already on.

You have something half-built that needs one boring step, the kind you keep skipping because it is not fun. Saturn is in the doorway, smiling patiently, holding out the screwdriver. Do the boring step. Then call or text Nancy and tell her the moon is in her sign and you did a responsible thing in its honour. She will be insufferable about it, and you will deserve it.
joel.mission: Do one dull, necessary step on a project today and announce its completion like a sports commentator.
joel.omen: Steam rising from a manhole or a vent in the cold. Quiet work underneath is about to pay off.
joel.stoneWhy: a warm stone for her moon

reading: Welcome home, Mountain. The moon in Capricorn is basically the sky moving into your guest room for two and a half days. Your instincts are sharper, your patience is longer, and your one-liners are deadly accurate. Enjoy it shamelessly.

Today your Life Path 11 picks up a signal that others miss: a coworker's real worry, a friend's unspoken plan, the exact moment a meeting should end. Act on it. Saturn, your ruler, is beaming with pride from the kitchen. The onyx bracelet on your left wrist, Joel's stone first, is warm to the touch even though it is cold outside. That is not physics. That is friendship.
nancy.mission: Trust your first instinct three times today, and keep a quiet tally of how many times it was right.
nancy.omen: A goat on a sign, a sweater, a mug or a cartoon. Your sign is waving hello.
nancy.stoneWhy: his stone, warm in the cold

together.text: Capricorn moon welcome party. Each of you names one way Nancy's steadiness made your year better, Nancy included. Joel goes first, because the Fire always speaks first. Nancy must accept every compliment without deflecting. Saturn is moderating, and Saturn is strict.

title: The Day of the Slow Kettle
skyStory: A six percent crescent climbs back into view, settling comfortably in Capricorn like it owns the armchair, which it now does. Capricorn moons do not hurry. This one is reading the sky's fine print and nodding. Mars knocks on the window asking if it can speed things up. The moon holds up one finger: wait. Mars, for once, waits.

reading: The Tiger wants it done by noon. The sky wants it done right. Today those two goals argue in the hallway, and the sky is going to win, so you might as well side with it early and look wise.

Something you are waiting on, a reply, a delivery, a decision from someone else, will not arrive today. That is fine. The [[Seven of Pentacles]] is leaning on its hoe in the garden, admiring the patch that has not sprouted yet. Do what it does: water it, look at it fondly, go inside. Use the spare energy to make someone else's day easier instead. That always sprouts fast.
joel.mission: When you catch yourself refreshing anything today, close it and do one kind thing for someone instead.
joel.omen: A kettle, pot or coffee maker that takes longer than usual. Good things are steeping, not stalling.

reading: Waiting is your art form. Other people think patience is passive. You know it is a skill, like whittling or poker faces. Today you get to show off, gently. Someone near you is fidgeting over a slow thing, and you can lend them your calm.

Around 2:45 pm, tell a story that has nothing to do with the stress at hand. A good one, with a twist at the end and maximum hand choreography. Your stacked diamonds will flash on the left middle finger at the twist. The fidgety person will laugh, forget the clock for ten minutes, and later tell someone you are their favourite. Saturn writes that down.
nancy.mission: Tell one great story today to someone who is stressed, purely to make them forget the clock.
nancy.omen: Waves rolling in at perfectly even intervals. Your steadiness is spreading to the people near you.

together.text: Slow-down challenge. Each of you picks one meal or drink today and takes twice as long as usual to enjoy it. No screens. Report afterwards the single best thing you noticed. Bonus points for something truly odd, like the shape of a cloud of steam.

title: The Day the Clocks Said Twelve Twelve
skyStory: December twelfth, twelve twelve, and the young crescent in Capricorn is eleven percent lit. Saturn has noticed the numbers lining up and is pretending it is not impressed. It is extremely impressed. The moon arranges the stars into a perfect row of twelve. Mars says that is showing off. The moon says yes. Tonight, coincidences have the right of way.

reading: Twelve twelve, and your Life Path 3 is humming because three goes into twelve perfectly. Today the universe is playing a matching game with you. At some point you will look at a clock exactly when it shows 12:12. Do not look on purpose. It will find you.

When it does, that is a DES moment, and the cabin requires a report. Message Nancy the exact time. Then expect a second match within the hour: a twelve on a receipt, a jersey, a house number. The [[Wheel of Fortune]] is spinning in a very small, very silly circle around you today. Ride it like a carousel horse with a goofy grin.
joel.mission: If you catch 12:12 on any clock today, stop and say Don't even scream out loud, wherever you are.
joel.omen: A house number, bus number or jersey with 12 on it. The universe is checking that you are paying attention.

reading: Life Path 11 on a 12/12 day, with the moon in your own Capricorn. You are running on pure intuition and it is uncanny. Someone will mention an old friend you were thinking about this morning. Then the friend will message you. ΔΕΣ, and you are allowed to scream a little.

The Wood Rat in you keeps a mental file on every coincidence, and today the file gets thick. Note the details: the time, the colour, what you were holding. The ruby on your right pinky flashes purplish-pink just as the second coincidence lands, like the stone is winking. Joel's fire knows you are getting the full show today. Enjoy the front row.
nancy.mission: Keep a tiny log of every coincidence today with times attached, then read the log aloud to Joel tonight.
nancy.omen: Twelve birds on a wire, or eleven and one late arrival. Either way, DES. You were meant to count them.

together.text: DES day, maximum edition. At 12:12 pm, wherever you are, each of you photographs whatever is directly in front of you and sends it without explanation. Compare the photos tonight. If both include something round, the universe is officially showing off.

title: The Day of the Upside-Down Umbrella
skyStory: The crescent swings into Aquarius at eighteen percent and immediately decides gravity is a suggestion. Aquarius is the sky's inventor, the one with goggles on its forehead and a screwdriver behind its ear. It has rewired the northern lights to play in a new colour called slightly-teal. Saturn, Aquarius's old co-ruler, sighs and fetches the fire extinguisher, just in case.

reading: Aquarius moon is a builder's moon, the weird kind. Today an odd idea will arrive sideways, probably in the shower or while scraping ice off the car. It will sound silly. Write it down anyway. Weird ideas are the ones that end up in the museum.

Your Life Path 3 wants to explain the idea to someone immediately. Wait twelve hours. Let it marinate. [[The Magician]] does not reveal the trick until the cape is ready, and your cape is still in the wash. Tomorrow, show it to one person. Nancy, ideally, because the Wood Rat will find the flaw and the fix in the same breath.
joel.mission: Write down the strangest idea you have today, then hide the note somewhere you will find it next week.
joel.omen: An umbrella blown inside out and still being used proudly. Odd shapes can still work just fine.
joel.stoneWhy: a little moon for big ideas

reading: Aquarius wants you to break one tiny rule today. Not a real rule. A habit rule. The way you always fold towels, the side of the bed you sit on to put socks on, the mug you always use. Switch one. See what the day feels like from a new angle.

Your diamond on the left ring finger is the Wind stone in your Captain Planet set, and wind loves a shake-up. By evening you will have a fresh opinion about something you thought was settled for good. Share it with full hand choreography. Someone will say huh, I never thought of it that way. That huh is your prize today.
nancy.mission: Change one small daily habit just for today, on purpose, and report how weird it felt.
nancy.omen: A snowman built upside down or sideways. The playful approach is the right one this week.

together.text: Invention hour. Together, invent one useless gadget for winter: a mitten that compliments you, a snow shovel that hums, a scarf with a weather report. Describe it in detail. Name it. Draw it badly. Aquarius will grant the patent tonight.

title: The Day of the Borrowed Thunder
skyStory: Aquarius keeps the crescent for one more day, now a quarter lit, and the moon has started a group chat with every planet. Mars sends thunder emojis. Saturn sends one thumbs-up, which is overwhelming enthusiasm for Saturn. Venus sends hearts. Mercury keeps typing and deleting. The moon reads every message and tells them all: something new is about to start. Nobody knows what.

reading: Something small and exciting starts today, and the cabin feels it in the floorboards. Maybe a new idea from yesterday's notebook catches fire. Maybe someone invites you into a project you did not expect. Whatever it is, give it a real yes.

There is a catch, and it is a friendly one. The [[Knight of Wands]] warns you that a new spark is only good if you have somewhere to put it. Before you say yes, decide what gets set down to make room. One thing out, one thing in. The fire burns brighter in a tidy hearth, and the cabin has been asking for a sweep for weeks.
joel.mission: Before saying yes to any new thing today, name one older thing you will pause to make room for it.
joel.omen: A spark jumping from a fire or a static shock off a doorknob. A new beginning has chosen you.
joel.stoneWhy: her fire for your new spark

reading: Mars and Saturn are getting along today, which is rare and noisy, like two thunderstorms deciding to share a valley. When they align, nothing can stop them, and you are going to feel that alignment as a sudden burst of energy around 11 am.

Use it on the thing you have been circling for a week. You know the one. The Wood Rat has already mapped every route to it and found the shortcut. The pearl on your right ring finger is the water in your five-stone set, and water carves canyons by not giving up. Today you just need to be water for one hour. Go.
nancy.mission: Pick the task you have been circling all week and give it sixty uninterrupted minutes before noon.
nancy.omen: Thunder in winter, or a sound like it from a truck or a door. Mars and Saturn just shook hands.

together.text: Mars and Saturn are aligned, so today you two are thunder. Pick one tiny shared project, a playlist, a recipe, a terrible poem, and each contribute one piece by midnight. Fire starts it. Mountain finishes it. Nothing stops it.

title: The Day of the Dreamy Fishbowl
skyStory: First quarter moon, a crisp half circle, floating into Pisces. Pisces is the sky's dreamer, the one doodling fish in the margins of every chart. The moon has gone soft and misty around the edges. Mars is trying to have a serious conversation with it and keeps getting distracted by bubbles. Saturn has given up and put on a bathrobe.

reading: A Pisces moon makes even the Fire Tiger a little sleepy, like a big cat flopped on a sunny rug. Do not fight it. Today your best ideas will come from staring out a window. That is not slacking. That is research.

Around 3:30 pm you will have a daydream so vivid you will forget what you were doing. Write down one detail from it. [[The Star]] is pouring water from two jars onto the ground, slowly, with no hurry at all, and the ground is happier for it. Be the jar today. Pour out a little, gently, with no agenda. The good stuff grows from that.
joel.mission: Spend ten minutes staring out a window with no phone and no plan, then jot one thing you dreamed up.
joel.omen: A fish anywhere unexpected: a sticker, a drawing, a weathervane. Your dreams are swimming in the right direction.

reading: The shore at first quarter has a softness to it, the fog rolling in low and silver over the water. Pisces is asking you to rest your sharp Wood Rat eyes for one day. You do not have to notice everything. You are allowed to just float.

The onyx bracelet on your left wrist is the Earth stone in your set, and today it is the anchor while the rest of you drifts. Take a long bath or a long walk or a long nap. Let your mind wander somewhere warm. By evening, the fog will lift and you will see something you have been missing, clear as a lighthouse.
nancy.mission: Take one long, slow break today with no goal at all, and refuse to explain it to anyone.
nancy.omen: Fog that lifts suddenly while you watch. A muddy situation is about to clear up on its own.

together.text: Dreamy day treaty. Neither of you is allowed to ask the other what you did today, only what you dreamed about. Share one daydream or night dream each. The weirder, the better. Pisces is listening and taking very bad notes.

title: The Day the Oars Got Lighter
skyStory: The moon is nearly half full in Pisces, still swimming through dreamy water, and tonight it is paddling a small rowboat across the sky. It is not lost. It is taking the scenic route. Saturn holds a lantern on the far shore. Mars rows alongside, splashing a little too much. Somewhere, a crossing that has taken all year is nearly complete.

reading: Today the [[Six of Swords]] floats into view, and it is not your card, it is Nancy's. The crossing she has been rowing all year is almost done. Your job is not to grab the oars. Your job is to be the lantern on the far shore, steady and warm.

Send her a message that has nothing to do with problems or plans. A memory, a joke, a photo of the cabin's smoking chimney. Let her know the shore is lit and the kettle is on. That is the whole mission. The Fire Tiger can sit still and glow today, which is harder for you than charging in, and so much more useful.
joel.mission: Send Nancy something warm that asks nothing of her, no questions, no plans, just a lit window.
joel.omen: A boat on a trailer, a boat on a sign or a boat in a painting. Her crossing is nearly complete.

reading: Look up from the oars. Seriously, look up. You have been rowing so long you forgot to check the view, and the view is good. The far shore is closer than you thought. There is a lantern on it, and someone you know is holding it.

The [[Six of Swords]] is reversed in your spread, a crossing not quite finished. But today it turns a little more upright. Let someone else row for ten minutes. Lean back. Look at the sky. The diamond on your left ring finger is your Wind stone, and the wind has finally turned in your favour. You are allowed to coast. You have earned it, and also you never had to.
nancy.mission: Let someone else take one thing off your plate today, and resist the urge to take it back.
nancy.omen: A lantern or a lit window seen from far away. Someone is waiting for you with the kettle on.

together.text: Rowboat check-in. Nancy names one thing that feels lighter than it did last month. Joel names one way to hold the lantern this week. No fixing. No advice. Just two old friends on opposite shores of the same small lake, waving.

title: The Day the Moon Visited the Tiger
skyStory: The moon crosses the halfway mark, fifty-five percent bright, and kicks open the door of Aries, Joel's home sign. It arrives with a battle horn. Mars, Aries's ruler, leaps up from the couch so fast it spills its cocoa. Saturn, watching from Capricorn, raises one eyebrow by exactly one millimetre. The snow on the ground looks suddenly ready for something.

reading: The moon is in your sign, Tiger, and you can feel it in your shoulders. Everything you say today lands a little harder and a little funnier. People will listen when you speak up. Pick your moment and speak up about the thing that matters most.

Aries moon makes you want to charge at five targets. The [[Knight of Wands]] from your spread is snorting in the stable, saying one, one, one. Aim the whole blaze at one goal today and watch it go up like dry birch bark. Then, tonight, switch the onyx to your right wrist and send a little of that fire to Nancy. She has a big week coming.
joel.mission: Pick the single most important thing on your plate and give it your loudest, boldest hour of the day.
joel.omen: A ram, a horn or a red door. Your sign is cheering and you are on the right track.

reading: The moon is visiting Joel's sign, which means the whole sky is feeling braver and a little more chaotic. You can borrow some of that Aries courage today. The Wood Rat has a plan that needs one bold first step, and today is the day.

Around noon, someone will ask you a question that deserves a fearless answer. Give it. No hedging, no maybe, no we'll see. The pearl on your right ring finger is your Water stone, but even water can be a waterfall. Be the waterfall for one sentence. Then go back to being the calm shore, because that is still your best look.
nancy.mission: Answer one question today without hedging. A clear yes or a clear no, delivered with a grin.
nancy.omen: Someone holding a door for you longer than expected. Your bold move is being welcomed.
nancy.stoneWhy: even water can be a waterfall

together.text: Aries moon brings courage, so today each of you tells the other one goal for 2027 that is so big it sounds silly. Say it out loud, no laughing. Then the listener says absolutely, and means it.

title: The Day of the Runaway Mitten
skyStory: Sixty-five percent of the moon blazes in Aries, and it has decided the whole sky needs a pep talk. It is shouting encouragement at the clouds. It has challenged Orion to an arm-wrestling match. It has taught the northern lights a new dance. Saturn is pretending to read in the corner, but its foot is tapping. Even Saturn can't resist an Aries moon.

reading: Second day of the moon in your sign, and the Tiger has energy to spare. Around 10:10 am, something will make you laugh so hard you need to sit down. Do not try to explain it to anyone. It was a private joke between you and the universe.

This afternoon a small, stubborn problem will refuse to budge. Do not push harder. Get playful with it. Sing at it. Draw it as a cartoon. Name it Gerald. [[The Fool]] is skipping along a cliff path with a tiny dog and a smile, and that silliness is exactly how stuck things get unstuck. Gerald will give up by 4 pm.
joel.mission: Give a stubborn problem a silly name today and address it by that name until it cooperates.
joel.omen: A lost mitten stuck on a fence spike, waving in the wind. Something you misplaced is about to turn up.

reading: Four days until your birthday, and the universe is already sneaking presents into the day. Small ones. A parking spot right in front. A song you love on the radio exactly when you get in the car. A stranger's dog that insists on saying hello.

Notice each one and say thank you under your breath. The Wood Rat may suspect a conspiracy, and the Wood Rat is right. The ruby on your right pinky, Joel's stone, is glowing a little brighter this week, like it is in on the birthday plans. It is. Do not ask questions. Let the surprises keep coming, and act surprised every single time.
nancy.mission: Count every small lucky thing that happens today, out loud, and announce the final total at bedtime.
nancy.omen: A dog wearing tiny boots, trotting like it owns the sidewalk. Birthday luck is warming up early.

together.text: Prank the universe back. Each of you secretly plants one small surprise for a stranger today: a kind note in a library book, a mitten lined up neatly on a post, an extra-generous compliment. Report your mischief tonight. The universe will be delighted.

title: The Day of the Sharpened Pencil
skyStory: The waxing gibbous, three-quarters bright, lingers in Aries for one last day and gets serious about it. It sharpens every pencil in the sky. It makes a list. It crosses things off with a satisfying flourish. Mars is impressed and slightly worried. Saturn nods approvingly, which in Saturn language is roughly a standing ovation.

reading: The moon is wrapping up its stay in your sign and wants you to finish one thing before it leaves. Not start, finish. The cabin has a half-built shelf, a half-written card, a half-sorted drawer. Pick one. By sundown, make it whole.

This is the Fire Tiger at its best: all that energy funnelled into one clean, satisfying finish. The [[Eight of Pentacles]] is hammering away at the workbench, happy as a clam in the repetition. Find that rhythm. Put on music. Get lost in it. When you are done, stand back and admire your work for a full minute. You are allowed to be proud.
joel.mission: Finish one half-done project completely today, then stand back and admire it for sixty full seconds.
joel.omen: A freshly sharpened pencil left on a desk. Today is a day for clean lines and finished work.
joel.elementWhy: a clean breeze through the cabin

reading: Three days to your birthday and the solstice, and the Wood Rat is in full preparation mode. You know exactly what you want those days to feel like. Write it down. Not a plan, a feeling. Cozy. Bright. Surprising. Pick three words.

Then do one small thing today to make room for those feelings. Clear a corner. Buy nothing; borrow a candle from a drawer. Send one message that will make the day easier. The stacked diamonds on your left middle finger catch the low winter sun, and every flash is a reminder: you deserve a birthday that feels the way you want it to.
nancy.mission: Write three words for how you want your birthday to feel, and tape them somewhere you will see daily.
nancy.omen: A wreath hanging slightly crooked on a door. Imperfect is perfect for your birthday week.

together.text: Countdown tune-up. Each of you finishes one thing today that has been nagging you for weeks. Report back with a one-word celebration. The goal is to walk into the solstice with lighter pockets and clearer heads.

title: The Day of the Fourth Cookie
skyStory: The gibbous moon, eighty-four percent bright, settles into Taurus like a cat onto a heated blanket. Taurus is the sky's homebody, the one who always has snacks and the softest sweater. The moon has stopped rushing. It is sniffing a cup of cocoa, admiring the frost patterns on the window. Mars tries to rally it. The moon just offers Mars a cookie.

reading: Taurus moon wants you to slow down and enjoy something with all five senses. The cabin smells like woodsmoke and cinnamon today. The floorboards creak in that friendly way. There is a blanket on the chair with your name on it, metaphorically.

Here is the [[Six of Pentacles]] lesson in its coziest form: let someone feed you, host you or take care of you for an evening. A friend's kitchen, a holiday gathering, a neighbour who insists. Say yes and do not offer to wash the dishes. Okay, offer once. If they refuse, sit back down and enjoy the fourth cookie. It is a gift. Receive it.
joel.mission: Accept one offer of hospitality today and sit down when you are told to sit down.
joel.omen: Frost on the window shaped like a tiny spruce forest. Comfort is on its way, probably carrying a blanket.
joel.stoneWhy: soft glow for a soft day

reading: Taurus moon is an earth sign, like you, and today feels like a deep breath after a long climb. Two days to your birthday. The shore is quiet. The waves are slow. Somewhere a pot of something good is simmering.

Let yourself be fed today, in every sense: a good meal, a long story from a friend, a nap in the afternoon light. The onyx bracelet on your left wrist is your Earth stone, and Taurus loves it, so you are doubly grounded. If anyone asks what you want for your birthday, say this exact feeling. Watch them try to wrap it.
nancy.mission: Let someone take care of you today without saying sorry for it even once.
nancy.omen: A pot steaming on a stove or the smell of baking drifting from a window. Abundance is closer than you think.
nancy.stoneWhy: Earth stone in an earth sign

together.text: Taurus moon feast. Each of you makes or orders something delicious today and sends a photo of it to the other. Describe the taste in one word. The other has to guess the dish. No winners, just snacks.

title: The Eve of the Longest Night
skyStory: The moon is ninety-one percent bright in Taurus, almost full, holding its breath. Tomorrow is the solstice and Nancy's birthday, and the whole sky is in on the secret. Saturn is wrapping a present with suspicious care. Mars is blowing up balloons and popping half of them. The moon is practising its brightest glow in the mirror. Everyone whispers: tomorrow.

reading: Tonight is the eve of the longest night, and the Fire Tiger is restless with anticipation. Tomorrow is Nancy's birthday and the solstice, the day the light starts coming back. You were born on the equinox; she was born on the solstice. You both arrived on turning points. Nobody believes that was random.

Prepare something small for tomorrow. A message, a memory, a plan. Not expensive, just true. The [[Two of Cups]] is raising a toast to old friendships, the kind that grow stronger every year. Tonight, switch your onyx to your right wrist and keep it there all night. Send the strength out. She will feel it at sunrise.
joel.mission: Write tomorrow's birthday message tonight, then sleep on it before sending it at sunrise.
joel.omen: The first star of the night appearing extra bright. Tomorrow's light is already on its way.

reading: Tonight is the last night of your current year, and the sky knows it. The moon is almost full, glowing over the shore like a lantern someone left on for you. The Wood Rat is curled up somewhere warm, thinking back on all the miles climbed since last December.

Take ten minutes tonight to name three things you are proud of from this year. Not just big things, small ones too. The time you said no. The time you said yes. The story that made a whole table laugh. The diamond on your left ring finger catches the almost-full moon. Tomorrow, the light comes back. Tonight, you rest knowing you earned every mile.
nancy.mission: Before sleep, name three things you are proud of from this year, out loud, to the ceiling.
nancy.omen: A candle flame that stands perfectly still. Your next year is starting calm and steady.

together.text: Eve of the solstice. Tonight, each of you sits in the dark for one minute, no lamps, just listening to the longest night. Then turn on one light together, at the same agreed time. That is the whole ritual. Tomorrow, the light returns.

title: The Mountain's Birthday and the Light Returning
skyStory: Solstice, full moon and Nancy's birthday, all stacked on one date. Don't even scream. The moon is ninety-seven percent bright in Gemini, the twins, winking at an equinox baby and a solstice baby who found each other. Saturn, her ruler, has put on a paper crown and refuses to take it off. Mars brought sparklers. At sunset, the sun turns around and starts walking home.

reading: Today the longest night breaks, and it is the birthday of the person who taught you that steady beats loud. [[The Sun]] from your spread has flipped upright for one day only, a limited engagement. Feel the joy without earning it first. Yes, Tiger, that includes you.

Around 4:30 pm, as the shortest day of the year sets, step outside and face whichever direction the shore is from you. Say happy birthday to the horizon like it can hear you. It can. Tonight is the Full Moon Recharge: the onyx goes on a moonlit sill, keeping a seat warm for the ruby. The chimney sends up one extra puff, purely for her.
joel.mission: Send your birthday message at sunrise, then keep the onyx on your right wrist until midnight.
joel.omen: Sunlight hitting something gold or silver at exactly noon. The light is choosing her today.
joel.stoneWhy: her stone, giving side all day

reading: Happy birthday, Mountain. The darkest night of the year ends on your birthday, and the light turns around and comes back. That is your entire personality as an astronomical event. ΔΕΣ, and also: obviously.

The [[Knight of Pentacles]] from your spread has been saying all year that joy is allowed, not earned. Today you are excused from earning anything. Let people fuss. Tell the long version of every story, hands up, all five stones flashing. At moonrise, set the ruby beside the onyx for the Full Moon Recharge: purple-pink fire, winter-black earth, solstice and equinox side by side. The sun comes back for everyone today. It just stops at your place first.
nancy.mission: Say yes to every birthday kindness offered today without a single but, really, or you shouldn't have.
nancy.omen: The full moon rising orange over the trees or the water. The light is officially returning.

together.text: Birthday, solstice and full moon in one night. Don't even scream. Each of you names one word for the coming year. Then, at the same moment, both stones under the same full moon. The light is returning, and you are both part of it.

title: The Night of the Full Recharge
skyStory: The moon reaches one hundred percent in Gemini, completely full, the brightest it will be all year. Gemini, the twins, holds two mirrors up to the sky, and the moonlight bounces everywhere: off snowbanks, frozen ponds, the windows of the cabin and the waves at the shore. Saturn takes off its party hat. Mars puts down its sparklers. Everyone just stares.

reading: Tonight is the true full moon, and the cabin glows silver in the snow. Yesterday was for celebrating. Tonight is for recharging. The Fire Tiger has been burning bright all year and the onyx has been working hard on your wrist. Time to let them both rest under the moon.

Before bed, place the onyx bracelet on a windowsill where the moonlight can reach it. Next to it, place something that reminds you of Nancy. Gemini loves pairs, so tonight the pair is everything. The [[Temperance]] angel is pouring water between two cups, perfectly balanced. Fire and Mountain, side by side under the brightest moon of the year.
joel.mission: Set the onyx on a moonlit windowsill tonight with one small token that reminds you of Nancy.
joel.omen: Moonlight so bright you can see your shadow on the snow. You are fully charged for the year ahead.

reading: The shore under a full moon is the most magical place in the world, and tonight it is yours. The waves are silver. The trees are black lace. The ruby on your right pinky looks almost violet in this light, glowing like it has been waiting all year for this exact moment.

Place the ruby on a windowsill tonight, beside the pearl and the diamonds, all five stones lined up like a tiny Captain Planet council. Earth, Fire, Water, Wind, Heart, recharging together. Gemini is the sign of twins, and you and Joel are twins of a sort: two turning points, two cardinal signs, two stones swapped.
nancy.mission: Line up all five of your stones on a moonlit windowsill tonight and leave them there until morning.
nancy.omen: A frozen pond or puddle reflecting the full moon perfectly. Your intentions are mirrored back.
nancy.stoneWhy: the little moon meets the big one

together.text: Full Moon Recharge, the real one. Both of you set your stones under tonight's full moon at the same time. Then text each other the same message: charged. That's it. That's the whole ritual. The moon will do the rest.

title: The Night of the Lit Windows
skyStory: Ninety-nine percent full, the moon drifts into Cancer, the sky's homebody, keeper of hearths and family recipes. It is Christmas Eve, and Cancer has turned on every lit window in the neighbourhood. The moon peeks into each one, approving. Saturn is reading a story aloud. Mars is trying to stay awake for something. Snow falls softly, as if it was scheduled.

reading: Cancer moon on Christmas Eve, and the cabin is at its absolute coziest. The chimney is puffing. The windows are glowing gold. There is something warm on the stove and something warm in your chest. Tonight is not for building or fixing. Tonight is for being home.

The [[Ten of Cups]] is painting a rainbow over the cabin roof, the picture of everything you have built finally just being enjoyed. Look around tonight, wherever you are, and take a mental photo. This is the good part, right here. You do not have to make it better. You only have to be in it.
joel.mission: Take one mental snapshot tonight of the warmest moment of the evening, and describe it to Nancy tomorrow.
joel.omen: A window glowing gold in the snow when every other window is dark. You are the light for someone tonight.

reading: The Wood Rat is curled up in the warmest corner of the house, tail tucked, ears still listening for the good stuff. Cancer moon makes everything feel like a hug today. Even the grocery line. Even the slush. Even the wrapping paper that refuses to tear straight.

Tonight, tell one story from a childhood holiday, the funnier the better. Use the full hand choreography; the stacked diamonds on your left middle finger will flash like tiny fairy lights. Someone will laugh so hard they have to wipe their eyes. That is your gift to the room tonight, and it is better than anything under any tree.
nancy.mission: Tell one funny holiday story tonight with full hand gestures, aiming for at least one happy tear.
nancy.omen: Snow starting to fall just as you step outside. The sky is setting the scene for you tonight.

together.text: Lit windows. At 9 pm tonight, each of you stands at a window with a light on behind you for one full minute. Think of the other. Fire in the cabin, Mountain at the shore, both windows glowing. Then go back to the warmth.

title: The Day of the Second Helping
skyStory: Christmas morning, and the moon is still ninety-six percent full, hanging low in Cancer like an ornament nobody wants to take down. Cancer has filled the sky with the smell of something baking. Saturn is in pajamas until at least noon, which has never happened before and may never happen again. Mars is assembling a toy with no instructions and loving it.

reading: Merry Christmas, Tiger. Somewhere today you will be handed a plate, a mug or a wrapped thing, and your instinct will be to deflect it toward someone else. The [[Six of Pentacles]] is sitting at the table with a napkin tucked in, watching. Take the plate. Take the second helping. Say thank you.

Around 3 pm, the day will hit that sleepy golden lull where everyone is draped over furniture like coats. That is the moment for one great story. Tell the one that always gets a groan and a laugh. Life Path 3, doing exactly what it was built to do: making a full room feel even fuller.
joel.mission: Accept a second helping of anything today, food or compliments, and do not apologize for it.
joel.omen: Someone falling asleep in a chair with a paper crown still on. The day is going exactly right.
joel.stoneWhy: gentle glow for a soft day
joel.elementWhy: a full table, a full heart

reading: Christmas at the shore: the water grey and silver, the snow on the dune grass, the smell of woodsmoke drifting from somewhere down the road. You have had your birthday, and now the second celebration rolls in like a gentle wave. You do not have to host this one in your head.

The Wood Rat sees everything at a gathering: who needs a refill, who is quietly overwhelmed, who wants to be asked about their new hobby. Today, pick one of those people and help them. Then, and this is the important part, sit down. The diamond on your left ring finger is reminding you that you are a guest at your own life sometimes too.
nancy.mission: Help exactly one person at today's gathering, then sit in the comfiest seat for a whole hour.
nancy.omen: Wrapping paper crumpled into a shape like a mountain. You are being honoured in tiny ways all day.
nancy.stoneWhy: you get to be a guest

together.text: Christmas exchange, no shopping required. Each of you sends the other a photo of the best thing you ate today and one sentence about the funniest moment. Whoever's story gets the bigger laugh wins bragging rights until New Year's Eve.

title: The Day of the Lion Nap
skyStory: The waning moon, still ninety percent bright, strolls into Leo, the sky's lion, all mane and confidence. After yesterday's feast, Leo has found the sunniest patch of sky and flopped down in it, belly up. The moon joins it. Saturn joins them both, which is frankly shocking. Mars paces for a while, then gives up and curls into a ball. Everyone naps.

reading: Leo is a fire sign like you, and today the big cats are all taking the day off together. The Fire Tiger has permission to sprawl. Find a warm spot, preferably near a window with a view of snow, and stretch out like you are being paid to.

If someone asks what you are doing today, the correct answer is lion things. The [[Four of Swords]] has fluffed a pillow and is pointing at the couch. You have been giving and building all month. Today, the only thing you are building is a nest of blankets. Recharge the fire. January will need it.
joel.mission: Take a real afternoon nap today, at least twenty minutes, and tell anyone who asks that it was mandatory.
joel.omen: A cat stretched out in a sunny window. That is your role model for the day.

reading: The Wood Rat is usually up early sorting leftovers and planning tomorrow. Today, Leo wants you to stay in bed a little longer. Let someone else make the coffee. Read a few pages of something. Watch the light move across the ceiling.

The ruby on your right pinky is Joel's fire, and Leo loves it, because Leo loves anything that glows. Hold it up to the window this morning and watch it go purple-pink in the winter sun. Your birthday week is still going, technically. Leo says the party lasts as long as you want it to, and today you want it to look like a nap.
nancy.mission: Stay in your pajamas until noon, read something purely for fun, and refuse all errands.
nancy.omen: A dog sleeping in a patch of sun. Rest is the right move today; follow the dog.

together.text: Lion day. Neither of you is allowed to do anything productive. Send the other a photo of your coziest nap spot. Best nest wins. Leo is judging on fluffiness, sunlight and number of blankets involved.

title: The Day of the Grand Entrance
skyStory: The moon, eighty-two percent bright, is still lounging in Leo, but the nap is over and now it wants an audience. Leo moons love applause. This one has put on a sequined cape and keeps walking in and out of the clouds for dramatic effect. Saturn is clapping politely. Mars is clapping enthusiastically. The moon bows. It does not stop bowing.

reading: Leo moon wants a show, and you are the showman. Today, make an entrance somewhere. Walk into a room like the music just started. Greet the neighbour like a long-lost friend. Wear the loud sweater. Your Life Path 3 lights up when people are smiling, and today you can make that happen just by arriving.

Around 6 pm, someone will need cheering up. Be the opening act. A ridiculous story, a silly voice, a dramatic retelling of your week with sound effects. The [[Page of Cups]] has a fish popping out of its cup and is giggling. Bring that energy. The cabin's chimney puffs a smoke ring shaped like a crown.
joel.mission: Walk into one room today like you are making a grand entrance in a movie, theme music optional.
joel.omen: A spotlight of sun breaking through clouds right on you. The stage is yours.
joel.elementWhy: a fresh breeze through the room

reading: Leo moon wants you in the spotlight, and today you will not even have to ask. Someone will turn to you at a gathering and say tell the one about. You know the one. Every friend group has a story only you can tell properly.

Tell it. Full volume. Maximum hand choreography. The pearl on your right ring finger, the stacked diamonds and the diamond will all flash at the punchline like a lighting rig. Leo will throw roses. The Wood Rat may pretend to be modest afterwards, but you will be smiling about it for days, and you should.
nancy.mission: Tell your best story today to someone who has never heard it, with full theatrical hand gestures.
nancy.omen: Someone calling your name across a room. Your audience awaits.

together.text: Leo stage night. Each of you performs one ridiculous thing for the other: a dramatic reading of a grocery list, a one-person play about your week, an interpretive dance of the weather. Video or live. Applause is mandatory. Roses are optional but encouraged.

title: The Day of the Empty Wishing Well
skyStory: The moon, seventy-two percent bright, slips into Virgo, bringing its clipboard back from the start of the month. It wants to review the year before it ends. It flips back through December, January, all the months, nodding thoughtfully and crossing off things that turned out not to matter. Saturn hands it a fresh pen. Mars fidgets.

reading: Virgo moon at the end of the year is a sorting moon. Today, look at the wishes you made this year, especially the ones you chased hardest. Some of them were real and some were the [[Nine of Cups]] from your shadow: shiny on the outside, hollow inside.

No need to judge the hollow ones. Just put them down. Thank them for the motivation and let them go. The Fire Tiger travels faster without the extra baggage. Write a short list of what actually made you happy this year, not what made you look busy. The real list will be shorter. It will also be better.
joel.mission: Write a list of what actually made you happy this year, then cross off anything that only looked good on paper.
joel.omen: A coin at the bottom of a fountain or a puddle. Some wishes were better as wishes; let them go.
joel.stoneWhy: her fire burns off the hollow

reading: Virgo moon is in an earth sign, like you, and it is doing what you do best: sorting. Today, review the year with your sharp Wood Rat eyes. What worked? What didn't? What deserves another shot, and what deserves a cheerful goodbye?

Wear the onyx on your left wrist like a compass today; it is your Earth stone, and it points true. Pick three things you want to keep in 2027 and three things you are leaving at the door. Say them out loud. The [[Eight of Swords]] from your shadow was a cage made of thoughts. Today, three of those thoughts get escorted politely to the exit.
nancy.mission: Name three things to keep and three to leave behind in the new year. Say them out loud.
nancy.omen: A door left slightly open. Something you are leaving behind has already started to go.

together.text: Year-end sort. Each of you names one wish from this year that turned out to be hollow and one that turned out to be gold. Swap. The listener says one sentence of encouragement about the gold one. The hollow one goes in the virtual bin.

title: The Day of the Identical Mugs
skyStory: Last quarter moon in Virgo, sixty-two percent bright, and the universe is in a playful mood. Virgo loves patterns, and today it has arranged a doozy. Two strangers will buy the exact same thing at the exact same moment in two different cities. The moon says it was not involved. The moon is lying. Saturn is trying not to laugh.

reading: Today's coincidence is going to be specific and ridiculous. Somewhere, maybe in a holiday photo, maybe at a friend's house, you will see a mug identical to one at Nancy's place, or one she mentioned. The exact one. Same chip in the handle, practically. DES. Send the photo immediately.

The [[Wheel of Fortune]] is spinning, and today it lands on the funny number. Nothing deep, nothing heavy, just the universe reminding you that you two are connected in weird little ways. The cabin's chimney puffs in amusement. Enjoy the strangeness. It is one of the best parts of having a friend this good.
joel.mission: When the coincidence strikes, snap a photo and fire it off to Nancy captioned only DES.
joel.omen: A mug, cup or bowl that looks exactly like one you know. Don't even scream, just document it.

reading: The Wood Rat sees patterns before anyone else, and today the universe is serving them on a silver platter. At some point, you will hear a word or phrase that Joel used in a message just this morning, out of a stranger's mouth. ΔΕΣ, and you will absolutely have to tell Joel before dinner.

Life Path 11 is a master number, and today you are its master. Write down every odd overlap you notice. By evening your notebook will look like a detective's corkboard, string and all. The stacked diamonds on your left middle finger flash every time a coincidence lands. Today, they are going to be busy.
nancy.mission: Keep a running list of every coincidence today and send it to Joel at exactly 9:00 pm.
nancy.omen: A stranger using a phrase that a friend said to you today. DES; the universe is quoting your group chat.

together.text: DES day, year-end edition. Tonight, each of you shares the single biggest Don't even scream moment of 2026. Then vote: which was more ridiculous? The loser buys the winner a hot drink, metaphorically or otherwise, in January.

title: The Day the Boat Touched Shore
skyStory: The half moon, fifty-one percent bright, steps into Libra, the scales returning for one last balancing act before the year closes. This time, the scales sit level on the first try. The moon looks surprised. Libra looks smug. Saturn and Mars, on opposite ends of the sky, nod at each other like two old sailors who have finally docked the boat.

reading: The year is nearly done, and the scales are balanced. All those days of giving, building, lifting, starting ten things at once: they added up to something real. Today, look back and give yourself the credit you would give a friend.

The [[Six of Swords]] has a little boat, and today it touches the far shore. That is Nancy's card, but you rowed alongside her this year, and you both made it. Send her one sentence about the crossing. Then do something kind for yourself, the giver. The onyx goes on your left wrist tonight, receiving side. Let something good come back to you.
joel.mission: Give yourself one compliment today, out loud, the kind you would give your best friend.
joel.omen: A boat pulled up on a snowy beach or tied at a dock. The crossing is complete, and it was worth it.

reading: Libra balances the scales, and today they tip in your favour. The crossing you have been rowing all year is complete. Look back at the water behind you. It looks calmer from here. It always does.

The diamond on your left ring finger is your Wind stone, and today the wind is at your back. Take a moment to stand on the far shore and look around. New ground. Solid footing. The Wood Rat sniffs the air and smells something good: next year, already cooking. Say one sentence of thanks to the oars, the boat and the friend who rowed beside you.
nancy.mission: Write one sentence about what this year's crossing taught you, then put it somewhere safe.
nancy.omen: Footprints leading up from the water onto solid ground. You have arrived somewhere new.

together.text: Crossing complete. Each of you names one way the other helped them get through this year. Be specific. Then a joint toast, coffee or tea or water, to the boat, the oars, and the friendship that kept it afloat.

title: The Night the Fire Met the Mountain
skyStory: New Year's Eve, and the moon is forty-one percent bright, a waning half in Libra, still holding the scales steady. Every planet has dressed up. Saturn wears a velvet jacket. Mars has sparklers in both hands and one behind each ear. The moon is counting down from ten, very slowly, savouring every number. At midnight, the scales tip forward into 2027.

reading: Last night of the year, and the cabin is ready. The fire is roaring. The windows are steamed up. Something warm is in your hand. You did a lot this year, Tiger. You started, you lifted, you gave. Tonight, you get to celebrate.

Before midnight, take out the scrap of paper Nancy gave you on December 1st, the one with her word for the month. Read it. Then write one word for 2027 and send it to her at 11:59. [[The Sun]] is rising on a new year. Let the joy come without earning it first. Happy New Year, Fire.
joel.mission: Send Nancy your one word for 2027 at exactly 11:59 pm, just before the year turns.
joel.omen: Fireworks bursting in red and gold. The fire is ready for the new year.
joel.stoneWhy: her fire for your new year

reading: The shore on New Year's Eve: the dark water, the cold stars, the warm windows behind you. You climbed a lot of mountains this year, Mountain. Some of them were literal. Most of them were not. All of them counted.

Before midnight, find the scrap of paper Joel gave you on December 1st. Read the word Joel picked for the month. Then pick your word for 2027 and send it at 11:59. The pearl on your right ring finger glows like a tiny moon, catching the fireworks. Happy New Year, Light Returning. The light already came back. Now it gets to stay.
nancy.mission: Send Joel your one word for 2027 at 11:59 pm, then watch the sky at midnight.
nancy.omen: The first firework of the new year reflected in water. The light is returning, and it is staying.

together.text: New Year's Eve. At 11:59 pm, send each other your one word for 2027. At midnight, both of you hold up your stones, ruby and onyx, toward the sky. Equinox and solstice. Fire and Mountain. Here is to the year ahead.
